subsections.subsection_title: IMPORTANT: NOT EVERY LONG INDUCTION IS A FAILED INDUCTION

blocks.text: This is one of the most important exam points.
The latent phase of induced labour can be prolonged.

ACOG notes that many women who remain in the latent phase for 12–18 hours after membrane rupture with oxytocin can still subsequently achieve vaginal birth. Therefore, in a reassuring maternal/fetal situation, Caesarean should not be performed prematurely simply because the latent phase is prolonged. ACOG

content_groups.group_title: Q2. Does unsuccessful induction automatically mean Caesarean?

blocks.text: No. The woman and fetus should be reassessed and options include rest and reassessment, expectant management, another induction attempt or Caesarean birth depending on the clinical circumstances and the woman's wishes. NICE

content_groups.group_title: Q3. What are the causes of failed induction?

blocks.text: Unfavourable cervix, inadequate uterine activity, malpresentation, malposition, fetal macrosomia, cephalopelvic disproportion, pelvic abnormalities, inadequate induction and occasionally an incorrect assessment of the original indication.

content_groups.group_title: Q5. What is the difference between failed induction and active-phase arrest?

blocks.text: Failed induction means labour has not been established after an appropriate induction attempt. Active-phase arrest means established labour has begun, but cervical dilatation subsequently stops despite adequate attempts at augmentation.

content_groups.group_title: Q6. At what cervical dilation does ACOG consider active labour to begin?
Q7. How long should you allow oxytocin before calling an induction failed?

blocks.text: “There is no single duration that applies to every patient. In an otherwise reassuring induction with ruptured membranes, ACOG recommends allowing at least 12–18 hours of oxytocin before diagnosing failed induction in the latent phase, with individualization according to the clinical situation.” ACOG

content_groups.group_title: Q8. What if the CTG is abnormal?

blocks.text: Stop/reduce oxytocin if appropriate, assess and correct reversible causes, obtain senior review and expedite delivery if fetal compromise persists.

content_groups.group_title: Q9. What if she has a previous Caesarean?

blocks.text: Carefully assess the type of uterine scar and discuss VBAC, induction, expectant management and repeat Caesarean as appropriate. Induction increases the risks of uterine rupture and Caesarean compared with spontaneous VBAC labour, so senior obstetric involvement is important. NICE

Whenever an examiner gives you a failed induction scenario, ask yourself:
“Is there an urgent reason why this baby or mother needs delivery now?”
That simple distinction will prevent many OSCE errors.

items: “How would you manage unsuccessful induction of labour?”

blocks.text: “I would first recognize that unsuccessful induction does not automatically mean Caesarean delivery. I would reassess the woman clinically, including vital signs, pain, bleeding and signs of infection, and assess fetal wellbeing with appropriate fetal monitoring.

I would review the original indication for induction and determine whether delivery is still required urgently. I would assess uterine activity, cervical dilatation and effacement, presentation, position, station, caput and moulding, and review exactly which induction methods have already been used.

I would distinguish failure to establish labour from active-phase arrest or obstructed labour. If maternal and fetal conditions are reassuring, management options include a rest period followed by reassessment, expectant management where safe, another attempt at induction, or Caesarean birth. I would discuss these options with the woman and respect her preferences.

If there is fetal compromise, maternal deterioration, infection, uterine rupture, obstructed labour or another urgent indication for delivery, I would escalate immediately and expedite delivery by the safest route.”
FAILED INDUCTION = DON'T PANIC → REASSESS → FIND THE CAUSE → DECIDE WHETHER TO WAIT, REPEAT OR DELIVER.
